facts.fact: The sally is voted in the black hour before first grey; the Company is human that night by rotation, so the fifteen smear then, turn, and fall back into the thorn at the village edge before first light. Kandan's ten follow on foot by the goat path.
facts.why: needed because odiyans cannot turn by day or fight in shape after dawn, yet the beat has the sally precede the village rescue.

facts.fact: The Company's vote is twenty hands to sixteen for the sally. Kamalakshi votes hold and then takes the shelf wall; Thulasi votes sally; Vellan volunteers.
facts.why: the beat requires a four-voice margin among the thirty-six remaining odiyans.

facts.fact: Devan announces the sally as his order under the Company's vote and tells Kandan his name goes first on the chalked tile of the dead if it fails.
facts.why: the beat has him lead it openly; the tile is Kandan's name roll of the dead (F820).

facts.fact: The Thurai vanguard horse lines (about seventy horses) stand at the mill ford below Kesu's village; torches come up the lower road behind them.
facts.why: places the horse lines the Company stampedes.

facts.fact: Ponni says she told Kesu the warden had a wife who ties knots; she asks Devan where Neela is.
facts.why: gives Ponni and Kesu a small reason to stay and ties to Neela's double hitch.

facts.fact: A Thurai boarding hook (iron, three-pronged, on a rope) tears across Devan's right ribs near noon in the lower narrows. He closes it with nine stitches of waxed silk using Kandan's curved needle. The long ladder-hook cut across his back from the previous day is still pulling.
facts.why: the beat's wound; the back cut matches Neela's welt in chapter 12.

facts.fact: Before she left, Neela told Devan she would go where the city was loudest; Devan reasons that in Kodiyur this means the noon gun, and so fears she may be on a stair at noon. He cannot warn her.
facts.why: the beat has him count the hour as the noon-gun day without having been told the plan.

facts.fact: Devan pricks his left thumb three times with the leopard tooth from his neck cord, about an hour after noon, to signal late that he lives.
